title: Letter to the editor concerning the article: Aknouche F, Magny R, Maruejouls C, Trebuchet C, Fargeot K, Thion L, Valancony C, Scherrer F, Oussedik ND, Kintz P, Labat L, Houzé, P. (2025) Systemic organophosphate poisoning in child following anti-lice lotion application. Journal of Analytical Toxicology, bkaf096
content: In their paper, Aknouche et al. have presented a very interesting case of diazinon poisoning. The child presented with symptoms of organophosphate poisoning and was treated with antidotes, although hypotonia, peripheral neuropathies, and respiratory disorders could not be prevented. The authors state that “These clinical signs, particularly hypotonia and peripheral neuropathies, may suggest the development of the intermediate syndrome associated with OP poisoning.” I think that muscular paralysis of the limbs of the patient reported in the author’s article should not be characterized as peripheral neuropathy. Peripheral neuropathy is a delayed neuropathy, and it is not observed within 96 hours after OP exposure but 2–4 weeks after poisoning, and the symptoms are mainly characterized by distal weakness and cramping muscle pain of both lower limbs, and it may also involve the hands. Distal numbness and paranesthesia occur as in all polyneuropathy cases, followed by depression of deep tendon reflexes in the lower limbs and, in severe cases, in the upper limbs [1, 2].
